class.name: HEGoPointUtil
class.brief_description: Point attribute maths shared by every handler that scatters something.
class.description: Multimesh instancing, object spawning and Terrain3D instancing all turn the same four point attributes into the same orientation. Each carried its own copy of that maths, with a comment promising to keep it in step with the others. It lives here instead, so they stay in step by construction.

method.name: basis_from_point
method.description: Orientation and scale for point [param index], from its N, up, scale and pscale. An N and up that are collinear leave no frame to build, so such a point keeps an unrotated basis. That is reported by [method is_orientation_collinear] rather than from here, so a caller can count the points it happened to and say so once instead of once per point.

method.name: transform_from_point
method.description: The transform for point [param index], oriented by [method basis_from_point] and placed at [param position].

method.name: is_orientation_collinear
method.description: Whether point [param index] carries an N and up that are collinear, which leaves no frame to build and gives the point an unrotated basis.

method.name: has_any_color
method.description: Whether these points carry a usable Cd attribute at all, so a caller can skip setting up per-instance colour when nothing would use it.

method.name: read_color
method.description: Reads Cd for point [param index], accepting both [Color] and [Vector3] and defaulting to white. Houdini hands colour back as either depending on how the attribute was created.

constants.constant: Attributes [method basis_from_point] reads. A point missing any of them falls back to the defaults below, so loading them is optional but everything ends up unrotated.
Attribute [method read_color] reads. Handlers that tint their output add this to [constant ORIENTATION_ATTRIBS]; object spawning does not, because it does not tint.
Direction a point faces when it carries no N.
Direction treated as up when a point carries no up.
